statement: You are given a binary tree with distinct values, the value target of one of its nodes, and an integer k. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
The distance between two nodes is the number of edges on the path between them; the path may go up through parents as well as down through children.

Return the values of all nodes at distance exactly k from the target. Any order is correct; here they are listed in the order a breadth-first search outward from the target reaches them, trying the left child, then the right child, then the parent of each node.

examples.explanation: Two steps down from 5, through its child 2, reach 7 and 4. Going up to 3 and then down the other side reaches 1.
3 is the root, so the nodes one edge away are just its two children.

constraints: target is the value of a node in the tree.
